title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool + parallel calls, result injection and retries
author: Priya Sharma
description: Motivation: customer workloads that invoke multiple tools in parallel exposed several ergonomics problems: (1) interleaved/partial tool outputs were difficult to re-inject into the model stream reliably, (2) retries for transient failures could cause duplicate side effects when tools were not idempotent, (3) the OpenAI compatibility layer mapped function_call semantics differently than our internal runner which led to surprising ordering and streaming behavior. This PR introduces a focused set of changes to improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool calls, durable result injection, and safer retry behavior. Main changes: 1) new ToolInvocationManager that centralizes per-request orchestration for multi-tool flows and maintains deterministic ordering policies while supporting parallel execution; 2) explicit injection_mode semantics (append|prepend|replace) for deterministic placement of tool results into the model input/stream; 3) per-tool idempotency metadata and a configurable retry_policy (none|idempotent-only|retry-once) enforced by the manager to prevent duplicate side effects; 4) streaming protocol updates so partial tool outputs are emitted as well-formed events that the streaming layer can forward to clients while the manager decides whether to inject them back into the model; 5) OpenAI compatibility shim updates that map function_call and tool results to the new injection semantics and preserve expected ordering for common patterns; 6) comprehensive unit + integration tests, and updated examples in the python and typescript SDKs. Backwards compatibility: default runtime behavior preserves existing semantics (injection_mode defaults to append, retry_policy defaults to retry-once for idempotent tools) so most customers see no change unless they opt into new flags. Migration: we added a short doc snippet and an example showing how to opt into replace-mode injection and how to mark a tool as non-idempotent. Impact: fixes streaming flakiness for multi-tool flows, reduces duplicate side effects on retries, and aligns OpenAI compatibility behavior with developer expectations. See commits and files changed below for implementation details.
